title: Getting started with GPAbin
text: Multiple imputation replaces missing value several plausible values, giving mm completed data sets instead one. Numerical summaries means regression coefficients combined Rubin’s rules. “summary” picture? construct biplot completed data set, get mm slightly different pictures. simply average coordinates, dimension reduction solution determined rotation reflection: configuration can come flipped, spun mirrored one imputation next. Averaging unaligned coordinates blur display nonsense. GPAbin solves three steps (Nienkemper-Swanepoel, le Roux Gardner-Lubbe, 2023): construct biplot every imputed data set; use generalised orthogonal Procrustes analysis (GPA) translate, rotate, reflect scale configurations onto common target; average aligned coordinates, mimicking pooling step Rubin’s rules, draw single unified GPAbin biplot. current version works categorical data, using multiple correspondence analysis (MCA) dimension reduction technique. resulting biplot, points represent samples / observations category level points (CLPs) represent response categories variable.

title: Getting started with GPAbin
text: use real survey data set included ca package: wg93, West German sample 1993 International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) environment. contains 871 respondents. Four questions (D) measure attitudes towards science five-point scale (1 = agree strongly 5 = disagree strongly) three demographic variables record sex, age group education. keep four attitude items together age group (six levels), giving five categorical variables. Take note: variables must factors; wg9

code: set.seed(2024) p_miss <- c(0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30, 0.40, 0.50)[as.integer(compdat$age)]  missdat <- compdat for (v in c("A", "B", "C", "D")) {   missdat[runif(nrow(missdat)) < p_miss, v] <- NA }  round(colMeans(is.na(missdat)) * 100, 1)   #>    A    B    C    D  age  #> 26.3 27.1 27.1 25.0  0.0

title: Getting started with GPAbin
text: missmi() entry point. checks data, records key dimensions percentage missing values creates object class missmi. printed summary reports: number imputations (m), number samples (n), number variables (p) percentage missing values (miss_pct). accepts either data frame containing missing values list already imputed data sets. data contain missing values, missmi() stops message, nothing impute.
code: missbp <- missmi(missdat) missbp #> [1] "Missing data with a total of 21 % missing values." round(missbp$miss_pct, 1) #>    A    B    C    D  age  #> 26.3 27.1 27.1 25.0  0.0

code: set.seed(927) missbp <- impute(missbp, imp.method = "miceB", m = 5) missbp$m #> [1] 5 anyNA(missbp$dataimp[[1]]) #> [1] FALSE

title: Getting started with GPAbin
text: DRT() (dimension reduction technique) runs MCA five imputed data sets. imputation stores sample coordinates (Z), category level point coordinates (CLP) level names (lvls). five solutions perfectly valid MCA, yet comparable: nothing forces five configurations share orientation. next step takes care .
code: missbp <- DRT(missbp)  length(missbp$Z)             #> [1] 5 dim(missbp$Z[[1]])           #> [1] 871  21 head(missbp$lvls[[1]], 6)    #> [1] "A:1" "A:2" "A:3" "A:4" "A:5" "B:1"

what: Step 4: Align and combine with GPAbin()
title: Getting started with GPAbin
text: core package. GPAbin() aligns m configurations generalised orthogonal Procrustes analysis averages aligned coordinates. Four new elements added object: see GPA , plot category level points five imputations (first two dimensions, one colour per imputation) alignment.  left, five MCA solutions scattered: every imputation produced differently rotated reflected picture, simple average meaningless. right, GPA, category level represented tight cluster five points. Averaging within cluster gives coordinates CLP.GPAbin. default centroid configuration used target. can supply G.target argument want align particular reference configuration.
code: missbp <- missbp |> GPAbin() stack_clps <- function(clp_list, stage) {   do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(clp_list), function(i) {     data.frame(Dim1 = clp_list[[i]][, 1],                Dim2 = clp_list[[i]][, 2],                level = missbp$lvls[[i]],                imputation = factor(i),                stage = stage)   })) }  clps <- rbind(   stack_clps(missbp$CLP,          "Before GPA"),   stack_clps(missbp$CLP.GPA.list, "After GPA") ) clps$stage <- factor(clps$stage, levels = c("Before GPA", "After GPA"))  ggplot(clps, aes(Dim1, Dim2, colour = imputation)) +   geom_point(size = 1.8) +   facet_wrap(~ stage) +   coord_fixed() +   scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set2") +   labs(colour = "Imputation") +   theme_void()

Dark points respondents; gold squares category level points, labelled variable:level. respondent tends answered question category whose point lies nearest . overall shape arch typical MCA ordered response scales: questions , B C extreme categories 1 5 lie opposite ends arch neutral category 3 sits apex. age groups found near centre display, age weakly related attitude responses. Take note: orientation biplot arbitrary: mirrored rotated version carries exactly information. plot() returns missmi object plot stored missbp$plot, can add like ggplot object:

title: Getting started with GPAbin
text: created missing values , know biplot complete data looks like. evaluation() performs MCA complete data supplied compdat, compares GPAbin biplot. possible simulation studies examples like one. table contains five measures: 1-PS: one minus Procrustes statistic. measures closely two configurations match best possible rotation. Values close 1 good. SP (similarity proportion): proportion responses category predicted GPAbin biplot equals category complete data. Observed responses kept , count correct construction (79% cells). missing cells actually predicted. , values close 1 good. RPR (response profile recovery): proportion respondents whose entire response profile recovered correctly. much stricter criterion SP, values close 1 reflecting successful recovery. AMB RMSB: absolute mean bias root mean squared bias two configurations. Smaller values better. hard interpret intended comparing competing approaches applied data. evaluation() also stores complete data coordinates compZs, compCLPs complvls, predicted categorical data sets GPApred compPred. can use draw two sets category level points top . orientation biplot arbitrary, first rotate GPAbin coordinates onto complete data solution small orthogonal Procrustes helper. following figure can constructed available output currently available package:  grey segment links category level’s position complete data biplot position GPAbin biplot. segments short: even quarter attitude responses missing, unified display stays close picture obtained missing data. largest displacements occur rarely chosen extreme categories (:5 C:5), hardest place many responses missing.
code: missbp <- evalMeas(missbp, compdat = compdat) missbp$tab #> NULL

title: Getting started with GPAbin
text: impute() convenience. prefer create imputations , example mice, pass list completed data sets straight missmi(). list recognised “already imputed”, impute() skipped. package also includes ready-made simulated examples, missdat (data frame 35% missing values), implist (five imputations ) compdat (complete data), handy trying functions quickly:
code: imp <- mice::mice(missdat, m = 5, method = "polyreg", maxit = 5,                   printFlag = FALSE, seed = 1) implist_own <- mice::complete(imp, "all")   # list of 5 completed data frames  own <- missmi(implist_own) |> DRT() |> GPAbin() own #> [1] "There are 5 imputations / variations of your data available." data(implist) missmi(implist) |> DRT() |> GPAbin() |> plot() |> evaluation(compdat = compdat)
